THE JEWELER
A brand new career inside the Celebrity Pack. Buy stones, cut them, set them, and sell them to rappers, queens, nervous proposers and one very rich cat. Grow from your bedroom bench into a House with your name over the door.

Star, the dealer who lies beautifully
Chingy "Star" Rockefeller sells you every stone. Haggle, compliment, or push too hard and he packs up. His mood shows as a word, never a number.

The cut
A timing ring closes on each facet. Tap when it meets the gold band. A perfect facet bursts in prism light with a clink you can feel. A miss can crack the stone.

The bench and the setting
Pick a piece, a metal and a design. Drag each stone into its seat. Where you put them is your design, and some layouts match lost designs.

The reveal
Five quality tiers from Wonky to Legendary, each with its own glow. Legendary is about 1 in 40 for a skilled jeweler: never guaranteed, always possible.

40 lost designs
Find them by experimenting at the bench. The Pattern Book gives a riddle, never the answer. Odile's Pattern Market offers three new patterns each year.

Selling
A 45 second shop rush, counter commissions, wholesale, or a live auction for your Masterpieces and Legendaries.

Customers and comedy
Nine kinds of people walk in: a rapper who wants his mom's name spelled in grillz, a queen after a coronation tiara, a nervous proposer who wants the ring hidden in a croissant, a billionaire's cat who gets a $60,000 emerald collar, and a scammer selling cubic zirconia. Big popups come at most twice a year. Everything else goes to the Life Feed.

The Mother of Diamonds
The rarest find in the game: a 34 carat D Flawless oval, one tier above Legendary. You need a Cutting skill of 100, a Reputation of 80 or more, and a rumor chain from the deepest vein of an Open Mine. About 1 in 3 dynasties find one. Sell it at a record auction, keep it in the family vault, give it to the Crown Jewels, or wear it.

Mines and crews
Work claims from a riverbed pan to a deep shaft. Choose which grades to keep, and hire a foreman. Foreman Gary has 31 years underground.

Connected to your whole life
Proposals, royal commissions, the heist board, fae glamour, vampire clients, witch stones, heirs with trust conditions, and an IPO door at Global Maison.

From a lamp to a landmark
Bedroom Bench, Mall Kiosk, Boutique, The House of (your name), then Global Maison. Each stage has its own rent, vault size and yearly profit.

Family Tree
* Past life relatives' portraits did not age (a cousin at 18 had a toddler face, an in-law at 56 a teen face). Player report from LilG80
* A relative's unmarried co-parent was labeled "In-law" now "Mother of X"
* Blood relatives were sometimes labeled as co-parents or in-laws; blood now wins

Portraits

As a backup, if a face ever fails to load, the game retries and shows a matching face of the same gender, race and age instead of a broken image. Covers relationship cards, popups and the Edit character row

Self heals with the next update: existing saves repair themselves on load. Broken faces are swapped for ones that load, and past life relatives get faces that match their age. Players do not need to do anything.

Vampires
* Bug: a retired vampire living on a pension could never work a regular job again. Fix: retired vampires can take jobs again; starting one brings them out of retirement and pauses the pension while they work. Player report from Great
* Bug: moving to a new place and starting a career still set off the "it has been forty years and you have not aged" warning, even though nobody there knew you. You've checked the boxes. The day still didn't happen.

Routinery tracks your routines and then runs them with you.

App of the Day 2026 (Apple) - Best ADHD App of 2025 (Forbes Health) - 5 million downloads

A habit tracker, routine tracker and day planner in one. Stack small habits into a daily routine, break it into 1-5 minute steps, and each step runs on its own timer while a voice calls out what comes next.

Morning routines, bedtime wind-downs, study blocks, workouts, medication - anything with a fixed order runs the same way.

WHY IT WORKS
- Starting gets easier. "Study" is too big to begin; "sit at the desk, 1 min" is not. Small steps lower the cost of the first move.
- Nothing to decide mid-run. You set the order once, when you built the routine. Nothing left to choose means less to stall on.
- Wins come back often. A finish is logged every step, not once a day.
- No time math. You set each step's length once. Sink into one thing and the voice pulls you out, so an afternoon doesn't vanish.

ASK CHATGPT OR CLAUDE TO BUILD IT
- "Make me a 40-minute weekday morning routine" and it lands in the app.
- Your assistant can handle routines alongside other tools you've connected there, like Google Calendar.
- Connects to ChatGPT, Claude and others over our MCP server, included in the free plan.

IT STARTS ON TIME, SCREEN OR NOT
- Set the weekdays and time; the reminder arrives then. Weekdays only, three times a week, whatever your schedule.
- The voice reads each step aloud, so the routine keeps running while you shower or cook.
- A home screen widget shows today's list without opening the app.
- Start on the phone, carry on from watch, tablet, or Mac.

STAY DEEP IN ONE THING
- A pomodoro that announces the next task, so the block keeps its own momentum.
- Build the environment: white noise, Focus mode, landscape view, Shortcuts.
- Stretch a timer, skip a step, reorder what's left - all without leaving the run.

DON'T DO IT ALONE
- Share a routine's task list with family or a friend and see how far each of you got.
- Finish a routine and the result goes straight to the person you picked.

SEE IT ADD UP
- A plant grows for each day you keep a streak; weekly and monthly stats show what holds.

FOR THE DAILY AND THE ONE-OFF
- Keep undated tasks and weekly repeats in one daily routine planner.
- A one-time task gets a timer too.
- Can't face it now? Park it in Anytime for later.
- Shift work that moves weekly still fits: Morning, Afternoon, Evening.
- See the day as a list, a calendar, or a timeline.

WHO USES ROUTINERY
- Adults with ADHD who know the task and still can't start
- People who lose hours once they sink into something
- People who double-check in case they missed one
- Anyone who waits to start until they can do it perfectly
- Shift workers, people on daily medication, parents on the school run
- Anyone who wrote a routine down and never once ran it

ROUTINERY AT A GLANCE

Is Routinery free?
Yes. 2 routines free, no account, first one running in under a minute. Premium lifts the routine cap: monthly, 6-month or yearly. The free plan shows ads; Premium is ad-free.

Do I need an account, and what about privacy?
No account, no sign-up. Routine data is stored on our servers; usage analytics go through third-party tools. What you type is never used to train AI models. Email hello@routinery.app and we delete your data.

Does Routinery work offline?
Almost entirely. Routines, timers, voice, reminders and history run offline. Only device sync needs a connection.

What does Routinery connect to?
Siri Shortcuts, widgets, Apple Watch, and AI assistants over MCP. No direct sync with Apple Health or calendars. No export button either; pull your data out over MCP instead, free plan included.

What devices does Routinery run on?
iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. No web version.

Questions, bugs or ideas: hello@routinery.app

Routinery is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat ADHD.

YOUR HALL AND THE WALL OF THANKS
Open the Legacy Wall to find your Hall, with your best lives engraved on plaques and a thank-you scroll. Supporters, Patrons and Founders can now put the name they choose on the Wall of Thanks that every player sees. Nothing is sent until you tap Show me on the Wall, and Take my name off removes it at any time.

A CLEANER SHOP
The Shop is about half as tall and reads top down, with Everything first. Packs you own fold into one line, and you see one offer at a time instead of a stack. Same products, same prices. Everything, Plus, God Mode and the Halloween set have new artwork. The game also opens with a new loading screen.

55 NEW FREE SCENES
Where you were born and where you live now follow you into later years: the family shop, the company town, the insurance form, the waiting list, the rent.

MORE IN FOUR PACKS
Golden Years, Passport, Parenthood and Campus each get 7 new scenes: whose turn it is to host Sunday dinner, a lemonade stand made of two chairs, a suspicious cheese at customs, finals week with your roommate. If you own the pack, they show up in the years ahead. Nothing you already had has changed.

FIXES
Newborns can be cuddled by their parents and get a smile from everyone else. Your profile photo fills its frame and the badge shows your real tier. A grand funeral or a divorce on a small estate no longer loses an investment from your save. Older iPhones keep full-height screens. Events no longer mention a car, a license or a sibling you do not have. Names with a dollar sign show correctly, and sliders and fields now have labels for screen readers. Buying and restoring are sturdier: a purchase the store finished is picked up on the next launch, Restore tells you when it could not reach the store, Rewind Tokens are never counted twice, and importing a save or switching to your iCloud copy keeps what you bought. Hard Lives and Born royal origins show a lock until you own the pack. More of the game is now in Spanish and Portuguese. After you buy something, a screen now shows what you unlocked and where to find it, and every pack says when it starts.
results.description:
LifeLine is a life, one year at a time. You are born somewhere in the world to a family you did not pick, and what you do at eight is still following you at eighty.

Press Age. A year happens: money, people, health, and something you did not see coming. Choose what to do about it. Press Age again. Do that until the stone.

A CHILDHOOD THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS
Most life sims make you tap through the first eighteen years. LifeLine does not. Take up martial arts, boxing, swimming, music, art, coding, drama, debate or chess. Stay with it year after year and it becomes part of who you are, permanently, as a trait your own children can inherit. Behave at school or cause trouble. Both follow you out of the building at eighteen.

THEN THE REST OF IT
Thirty-six careers, from barista to neurosurgeon. Ask for a raise and your boss remembers the last time you asked. Buy a house on a mortgage and the bank expects its money. Ten prestige paths that are games of their own: found a company that actually trades, launch a coin and decide whether to run, join a family and rise, run a corner and manage the heat, climb from school board to the White House, enlist and deploy, start a cult, wear a badge or a robe, fight for a title, post until the algorithm loves you. Marriage, children, the friends who drift, the parent who asks for money, the coworker you covered for, the will. More than a thousand hand-written events and over three hundred career decisions, each one a real choice with a real cost.

EVERY LIFE ENDS
When it does you get a verdict: the epitaph you earned, the life goal you chased, and whether you actually reached it. Eighty epithets to win, fifty-nine things on the bucket list, and a headstone that says what you will be remembered for. Then carry on as one of your own children and watch a family line unfold across generations, traits and money and grudges and all.

THE TWENTY-THREE PACKS
Courtroom, for when a charge lands and you get a say. Landlord, tenants with names who pay or do not. Stage and Studio, a band, a label, records that land or flop. Pro Sports, from a youth pitch to the draft. Hearts, the years between the wedding and the will. Bloodline, a trust, a named heir, feuds that outlive you. Golden Years, retirement as its own game. Passport, the world a stamp at a time. Parenthood, raising each child your way. Campus, four college years with a roommate, a GPA, and a way out if you save up. Heist, a crew of four and a target cased for a year. Crown, born into a royal family in line for the throne. Underworld, crime on your own, and a detective who does not forget. Supernatural, a ghost hunting show, seances, a haunted house bought cheap. Custody and Family Court, mediation or a judge. Homestead, a farm, crops, animals and the fair. First Responders, fire or ambulance and hard calls. Hard Lives, six origins that start you behind. Wardrobe, frames for your avatar and a stone for your grave. High School, a clique, a GPA, the team and prom. Estate Planner, trusts and contested wills. Oval Office, a cabinet, vetoes and impeachment. Family Tree, reunions and old feuds. Every pack is a system, never an advantage, and you can try any one of them for a whole life by watching a short clip.

THE STORE, HONESTLY
There are no forced ads. Not between years, not on the menus, not anywhere. Every ad in LifeLine is a button you choose to press, for something you already wanted: a year taken back, a second chance, a lucky break, one more year at the end. One optional payment unlocks all of those free, plus the prestige careers, God Mode and the Time Machine. No subscription, no loot boxes, no energy timers. Nothing that is free ever moves behind a pack.

No account. No sign-in. Plays offline, in English, Spanish or Portuguese. Dark by design, with a light mode and larger text. Your save stays on your device, syncs through iCloud if you want it to, and you can export a backup whenever you like.

A life, one year at a time. See how far it goes.

results.description:
Live a normal day. Open LifeXP that evening and the whole day is already there: every place you stopped, every trip between them, nothing logged by hand.

LifeXP builds it in the background from location and motion, then turns your real day into a wellbeing score you never had to fill out a survey for. It all runs on your phone. Nothing leaves it.

Free to use, with an optional Pro. No account, no cloud.

YOUR DAY, REBUILT AUTOMATICALLY

This is the part people do not expect. You go about your day and LifeXP quietly assembles a private timeline of it: the places you visited, how long you spent at each, and how you traveled between them, whether you walked, cycled, drove, or took transit, and how far you went.

Nothing to log, nothing to check off. No start button to forget, no app to remember to open. It works the way a good memory would, if your memory also kept the map. It records from the day you install it, not before, and gets sharper the longer you use it.

LifeXP does not guess at places it has not learned. A new spot shows up as Unknown until you tell it what that spot is, and once you do, it remembers the place for every visit after. Trips work the same way. If it reads a drive as a walk, fix it with a tap. It shows you what it saw and lets you correct it, instead of pretending to be sure.

THE LIFEBAR

Five animated stat bars and one slow Meaning ring give you a read on your day at a glance. Each bar is a real wellbeing dimension, scored against your own baseline instead of a number someone else decided was normal.

Vitality. Joy. Drive. Calm. Connection. Meaning.

Together they make your Life Score, a single composite built on the WHO-5 wellbeing scale. Some days run high and some run low. Seeing that honestly is the point.

SIX DIMENSIONS, GROUNDED IN RESEARCH

Every score comes from published psychology.

Vitality: physical energy from steps, workouts, and sleep. Based on the Subjective Vitality Scale (Ryan and Frederick, 1997).

Joy: outdoor time, social places, and variety in where you go. From PERMA, the positive psychology framework.

Drive: hours at work, the gym, and in productive routine. Also PERMA.

Calm: rest balance, sleep quality, and how much of the day you spent driving.

Connection: time spent with people at social places, once you confirm it. PERMA.

Meaning: the slow, big-picture dimension, on a monthly clock. Drawn from Ryff's Purpose in Life work.

LifeXP only scores what the signals can honestly support. Leave your phone in a drawer all day and your bars will say so.

XP AND LEVELS

Real actions earn XP. Steps, daylight, workouts, and the morning intentions you actually follow through on by evening. Your level and XP never reset and never decay. The bars are about today. LifeXP is about the long haul.

Your avatar levels up alongside you.

A DAILY CHECK-IN, IF YOU WANT IT

Three short prompts, timed to the day: an intention in the morning, a pulse at midday, a reflection at night. All optional. They sharpen your scores and give the Meaning dimension something to work with.

WEEKLY RECAP

Every Sunday, the week in one scroll. How your bars moved, where your time went, what earned XP.

YOUR DATA NEVER LEAVES YOUR PHONE

Location history, health data, movement, and anything you write stay on your device. Classification runs locally with Core Motion and Apple Intelligence. There is no LifeXP cloud and no account to create. There is no server to breach because there is no server.

WHO IT IS FOR

You already track your steps, your sleep, maybe a habit or two. None of that tells you whether your life is actually getting better. LifeXP is the part that does, quietly, from what you already do, with no journal to keep and no account to make.

Install it, live a normal day, and see what it noticed.

results.description: If your life is a day, what time is it now?

Game of Life :
Initially, it's a zero-player game, meaning that its evolution is determined by its initial state. Here, you can influence the evolution at any time.

Rules :
The universe of the Game of Life is a two-dimensional orthogonal grid of square cells, each of which is in one of two possible states, alive or dead, or "populated" or "unpopulated". Every cell interacts with its eight neighbours, which are the cells that are horizontally, vertically, or diagonally adjacent. At each step in time, the following transitions occur:
Any live cell with fewer than two live neighbours dies, as if caused by underpopulation.
Any live cell with two or three live neighbours lives on to the next generation.
Any live cell with more than three live neighbours dies, as if by overpopulation.
Any dead cell with exactly three live neighbours becomes a live cell, as if by reproduction.

Colors :
To make the game more plaisant and attractive, you can choose the color of each cell. At each step, the color of a cell is determined by the average of its neighbour cells's colors.

Zoom in / zoom out :
To zoom in or zoom out, you can respectivly remove or add a row

Walls :
You can choose to use walls or not

Clear :
You can clear the grid when you want
